responses.text: The ToString method converts an object to its string representation using a specified format and format provider. This public instance method overload accepts two parameters: a format string that defines how the output should be structured, and an IFormatProvider that supplies culture-specific formatting information. The method returns a string containing the formatted representation of the object. This overload enables developers to obtain culture-aware and fully customizable string formatting for type conversion operations, accommodating diverse international requirements and custom formatting preferences for global software applications.

Converts the current object to its string representation using the specified format string and format provider.

Parameters:
format: A format string that specifies the desired format of the returned string representation, controlling how the object is formatted.

formatProvider: An object that implements IFormatProvider and provides culture-specific formatting information, supplying formatting conventions for the current culture or custom format specifications.

Returns:
A string that represents the current object, formatted according to the specifications provided by the format parameter and the formatting conventions supplied by the formatProvider parameter.

Formats the value of the current instance using a specified format and culture-specific formatting information. The format parameter specifies the desired format to use, or can be a null reference to use the default format for the type implementing IFormattable. The formatProvider parameter specifies the format provider to use for formatting values, or can be a null reference to use numeric format information from the operating system's current locale setting. This method returns the formatted value of the current instance in the specified format.

Formats the value of the current instance using the specified format string and format provider settings. The format parameter specifies the exact format string to be applied, or a null reference to use the default format defined for the IFormattable implementation type. The formatProvider parameter specifies the specific format provider to use for the formatting operations, or a null reference to obtain the numeric format information from the current operating system's locale settings. Returns the value of the current instance in the specified format.

MarkZshCompPositionalArgumentFile configures Zsh shell completion behavior for a specific positional command argument to enable file completions. The argPosition parameter specifies which positional argument position to configure using zero-based indexing. The patterns variadic parameter accepts one or more file glob patterns that filter and limit which files are offered as possible completion candidates. Returns an error if the configuration operation fails.

MarkZshCompPositionalArgumentFile configures a positional argument for Zsh shell completion to complete as file paths. The argPosition parameter specifies the positional argument position using zero-based indexing. The patterns parameter accepts one or more glob patterns to filter and present matching files to the user during shell tab completion. The method returns an error if the configuration operation fails.

MarkZshCompPositionalArgumentFile only worked for zsh and its behavior was inconsistent with Bash completion. It has therefore been disabled. Instead, when no other completion is specified, file completion is now done by default for every argument. One can disable file completion on a per-argument basis by using ValidArgsFunction and ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp. To achieve file extension filtering, one can use ValidArgsFunction and ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt.

MarkZshCompPositionalArgumentFile, which only worked in zsh and exhibited behavior inconsistent with Bash completion, has been disabled. File completion is now enabled by default for all arguments when no other specific completion type is specified. You can disable file completion on a per-argument basis by using ValidArgsFunction with ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp. To achieve file extension filtering, use ValidArgsFunction with ShellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt.

Creates a LogEventPropertyValue from the provided object. Accepts an object value parameter for conversion into a property value representation. The destructureObjects boolean parameter (default false) determines whether complex objects should be destructured during the conversion process. When set to false, objects remain fully preserved as-is. Returns a LogEventPropertyValue instance representing the input object value.

Creates and returns a LogEventPropertyValue instance from the provided object value. Accepts an object parameter and an optional boolean destructureObjects flag (defaults to false) that controls whether complex objects are destructured into their individual constituent properties. When destructureObjects is false, the given object is preserved as a single value without any further decomposition or modification.

Creates a LogEventPropertyValue from a .NET object using the specified destructuring strategy. The value parameter represents the property value to be converted. If destructureObjects is true and the value is a non-primitive, non-array type, it will be converted to a structure; otherwise, unknown types will be converted to scalars, typically stored as strings.

<summary>Creates a LogEventPropertyValue from a .NET object according to the specified destructuring strategy.</summary>
<param name="value">The property value to be converted.</param>
<param name="destructureObjects">If true, non-primitive and non-array values are converted to structures; if false, unknown types are converted to scalar values, which are typically stored as strings.</param>
<returns>A LogEventPropertyValue instance representing the final converted value.</returns>

SuiteTester is a struct type with no parameters required for instantiation or use. The type name suggests it provides functionality for testing and managing test suites. As a parameter-free struct, it offers straightforward implementation for developers. The minimal initialization requirements allow flexible usage across various testing scenarios. This struct type serves as a core component in testing frameworks.

SuiteTester is a struct type for test suite management and execution. It provides core functionality for organizing and running multiple test suites within a testing framework. The type itself has no defined parameters or numeric constants. SuiteTester serves as a container type enabling full implementation of comprehensive test suite capabilities and supporting the efficient execution of organized test operations.

This suite is intended to store values and ensure that only testing-suite-related methods are executed. It is also a fully functional example of a complete testing suite, using both setup and teardown methods as well as a helper method that is ignored by testify framework. To effectively reflect real-world testing practices, all tests in the suite perform an assertion.

This suite stores values to ensure that only testing-suite-related methods run. It is also a fully functional example of a testing suite, using setup and teardown methods and a helper method that is ignored by testify. To represent real-world scenarios more accurately, all tests in the suite perform various types of assertions to properly validate the expected behavior outcomes.

PushProperty pushes a named property onto the property stack for the current logical scope. It accepts three parameters: a property name as a string, a value as an object, and an optional boolean parameter destructureObjects that defaults to false. When destructureObjects is true, the value object is destructured for detailed representation and inspection purposes; when false, the object is treated as a single, undecomposed value without structural analysis. The method returns an IDisposable object that manages the property's lifecycle within the scope. Disposing the returned object pops the property from the stack, removing it from the scope and ensuring automatic cleanup upon disposal. This scoped property pattern is useful for managing temporary context-specific data with guaranteed resource cleanup behavior.

PushProperty creates a disposable context that adds a property to the current scope with the specified name and value. The method is static and returns an IDisposable, enabling use with using statements for automatic cleanup when the context exits. The name parameter specifies the property identifier, while the value parameter contains the data to be pushed. The destructureObjects parameter controls object handling behavior; when set to true, objects are destructured, and when false (the default), they are preserved as-is. Disposing the returned IDisposable removes the pushed property from the scope, restoring the previous state.

```xml
<summary>
Pushes a property onto the context stack and returns an IDisposable handle that must be disposed to remove the property and any other properties stacked on top of it that have not yet been popped. The property must be popped from the same thread or logical call context in which it was pushed.
</summary>
<param name="name">The name of the property to push onto the context stack.</param>
<param name="value">The value of the property to push onto the context stack.</param>
<param name="destructureObjects">If true, non-primitive, non-array type values are converted to a structured representation; otherwise, unknown types are converted to scalar values, which are generally stored as strings.</param>
<returns>An IDisposable token that must be disposed to pop the property and all stacked properties from the context stack.</returns>
```

Push a property onto the context, returning an <see cref="IDisposable"/> that must be disposed to remove the property and any others stacked above it but not yet popped. Properties must be popped from the same thread or logical call context.

<param name="name">The name of the property.</param>
<param name="value">The value of the property.</param>
<param name="destructureObjects">If true and the value is a non-primitive, non-array type, the value will be converted to a structure; otherwise, unknown types are converted to scalars, typically stored as strings.</param>
<returns>A disposal token that pops properties from the stack in order.</returns>

NewRandom generates a new randomly generated UUID value. The function takes no parameters and returns both a UUID value and an error value. The error indicates whether the UUID generation succeeded or failed. Call this function to obtain a new UUID value for use in applications requiring globally unique identifiers for their various data objects.

NewRandom generates and returns a new random UUID value along with an error. The function accepts no parameters and returns a tuple containing a UUID and an error value. On successful generation, the error is nil. On failure, a non-nil error describing the underlying cause is returned. Use NewRandom to generate new random UUID instances.

Randomly generated UUIDs have 122 random bits. The annual human risk of being struck by a meteorite is approximately one in 17 billion—corresponding to a probability of 6 × 10−11. This collision probability is equivalent to the odds of creating a few tens of trillions of UUIDs in a single year and experiencing one duplicate.

Randomly generated UUIDs contain 122 random bits of entropy. The estimated annual human risk of meteorite impact is approximately one in 17 billion, equivalent to a probability of 6 × 10−11. Generating tens of trillions of UUIDs in a single calendar year would likely result in approximately one collision, thus closely matching this risk level.

GenMarkdownTree generates markdown documentation for a Cobra command and its associated subcommands, writing the complete output tree structure to the specified directory. The function accepts a cobra.Command pointer and a target directory path as input parameters. It returns an error if the operation fails, such as when the function is unable to write files to disk or properly traverse the command hierarchy.

GenMarkdownTree generates markdown documentation from a Cobra command and writes the output to a specified directory. It accepts a pointer to a Cobra Command and a target directory path as parameters. Returns an error if the operation fails, such as when unable to create output files, write to the directory, or if the directory path is invalid or becomes inaccessible to the function.

GenMarkdownTree generates a markdown page for a command and all its subcommands in a given directory. The header may be nil. This function may not work correctly if command names contain hyphens. For example, if you have `cmd` with subcommands `sub` and `sub-third`, where `sub` also has a subcommand called `third`, it is undefined which help output will be in the file `cmd-sub-third.1`.

GenMarkdownTree generates a markdown page for this command and all its descendants in the specified directory. The header may be nil. This function may not work correctly if your command names contain hyphens. If you have `cmd` with two subcommands, `sub` and `sub-third`, and `sub` has a subcommand called `third`, it is undefined which help output will be in the file `cmd-sub-third.1`.

Schemes is a method on the Route type that modifies the route's schemes configuration. It accepts a variadic parameter schemes of type string, allowing one or more schemes to be easily specified in a single method call. The method returns a pointer to the Route receiver, enabling method chaining for fluent configuration. The variadic parameter design allows developers to specify multiple schemes without requiring multiple separate method invocations, making the API more convenient and ergonomic for supporting many common usage patterns effectively.

Schemes configures the HTTP schemes accepted by this specific route. It accepts a variadic parameter of strings, where each represents a scheme such as "http" or "https", constraining which protocol types the route matches. Multiple schemes may be specified in a single call. The method returns a pointer to the receiver Route, enabling fluent method chaining capabilities. This allows composing full route configurations using builder-style patterns where multiple configuration methods are chained together sequentially to define complete, custom route specifications and configurations.

Schemes adds a matcher for URL schemes. It accepts a sequence of schemes to be matched, such as "http" and "https". If a request's URL has a scheme set, it will be matched against. Generally, the URL scheme is set only if a previous handler sets it, such as the ProxyHeaders handler from gorilla/handlers. If unset, the scheme value will be determined based on the request's TLS termination state. The first argument to Schemes will be used when constructing a route URL.

Schemes adds a matcher for URL schemes. It accepts a sequence of schemes to match, such as "http" or "https". If the request's URL has a scheme set, it is matched against that scheme. The URL scheme is typically set by a previous handler, such as the ProxyHeaders handler from gorilla/handlers. If the scheme is not set, it is determined from the request's TLS termination state. The first argument to Schemes is used when constructing a route URL.

The `fallthrough_msg` variable stores a formatted error message generated by the `format!` macro. This message is constructed when deserialized data does not match any variant of an untagged enum. The message includes the enum's type name, obtained via `params.type_name()`, to provide context about which specific enum type failed to deserialize properly. This error occurs during deserialization when input data cannot be matched against any of the defined variants of the untagged enum.

The `fallthrough_msg` variable creates a formatted error message when data fails to match any variant of an untagged enum during deserialization processing. It uses Rust's `format!` macro to construct the error string message, incorporating the enum's type name through `params.type_name()`. This fallback error message is then emitted when no enum variant successfully deserializes the provided input data, enabling developers to identify which specific untagged enum type caused the deserialization failure to occur.

The TOML error handling mechanism could be improved by saving the errors from all failed parsing attempts. Currently, the heuristic used by TOML counts the total number of fields processed before an error and reports only the error that happened after the largest number of fields were processed. An alternative approach would be to save all the errors encountered and combine them into one message that explains why none of the variants matched.

TODO: Improve error reporting by preserving all errors from failed parsing attempts rather than discarding them immediately. The current TOML parsing heuristic counts the number of fields processed before each error occurrence and returns the error from the attempt that processed the most fields overall. Consider instead combining all collected errors into a single consolidated message that clearly explains why none of the variant parsers successfully matched the provided input data.

Wraps an ILogEventEnricher by applying a transformation function and additional configuration to the logging enrichment pipeline. This static method accepts a LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration instance, a Func<ILogEventEnricher, ILogEventEnricher> delegate that transforms enricher objects during pipeline processing, and an Action<LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration> to configure the wrapped enricher settings and options. Returns a configured LoggerConfiguration instance suitable for logger pipeline construction and use.

Wraps a logger enricher with a custom decorator function and applies configuration to the wrapped enricher. The wrapEnricher parameter provides a transformation function that accepts an ILogEventEnricher instance and returns a newly decorated ILogEventEnricher. The configureWrappedEnricher action enables additional enrichment pipeline configuration and initialization setup. Returns the modified LoggerConfiguration object supporting fluent method chaining throughout the logger setup process.

<summary>Helper method for wrapping log event enrichers.</summary>
<param name="loggerEnrichmentConfiguration">The parent enrichment configuration.</param>
<param name="wrapEnricher">A function that wraps ILogEventEnrichers added by configureWrappedEnricher.</param>
<param name="configureWrappedEnricher">An action that configures enrichers to wrap.</param>

Helper method for wrapping enrichers within a logger enrichment configuration. Accepts the parent enrichment configuration, a wrapping function for ILogEventEnrichers, and an action configuring enrichers for wrapping. Returns a configuration object supporting method chaining for fluent API patterns and continued configuration setup. Throws ArgumentNullException if any of the required loggerEnrichmentConfiguration, wrapEnricher, or configureWrappedEnricher parameters are null.

The `tp` pointer references character data for traversing or storing the address string. This pattern is used in network address formatting operations where a fixed buffer holds the ASCII representation of an IPv6 address.

Declares a character array tmp sized by the constant UV__INET6_ADDRSTRLEN and a character pointer tp. The tmp array and tp pointer are suitable for storing and manipulating IPv6 address string data. UV__INET6_ADDRSTRLEN defines the required buffer size for IPv6 address string representation in network operations. The numeric constant 16 is associated with this structure. LogEvent initializes a new log event with specified parameters. The constructor accepts a DateTimeOffset timestamp indicating when the event occurred, a LogEventLevel level defining the severity, an Exception exception for error details, a MessageTemplate messageTemplate containing the log message format, and an EventProperty[] properties array holding contextual data. This internal constructor properly combines all required information for structured logging event operations.

LogEvent is an internal constructor that accepts DateTimeOffset timestamp, LogEventLevel level, Exception exception, MessageTemplate messageTemplate, and EventProperty array properties. It initializes a log event with these parameters. The timestamp represents event occurrence time as a DateTimeOffset, level specifies the LogEventLevel, exception contains exception information, messageTemplate provides the message template, and properties holds the array of EventProperty values associated with the event.

Construct a new . The time at which the event occurred. The level of the event. An exception associated with the event, or null. The message template describing the event. Properties associated with the event, including those presented in . Thrown when is null or when is null.

Constructs a new LogEvent instance. The timestamp parameter specifies when the event occurred. The level parameter indicates the event severity level. The exception parameter optionally provides an associated exception. The messageTemplate parameter provides a template describing the event details. The properties parameter contains event properties, including those referenced in the message template. ArgumentNullException is thrown if messageTemplate or properties is null.

Renders log event properties to a TextWriter. Accepts an IReadOnlyDictionary mapping string keys to LogEventPropertyValue objects, along with a TextWriter destination and optional IFormatProvider for controlling output formatting behavior during rendering operations. When the IFormatProvider parameter is not specified, it defaults to null. This public void method processes and outputs formatted structured log event property data to the specified TextWriter output destination for consumer applications and integrated logging frameworks.

Renders log event properties to a specified TextWriter output destination. The method accepts a read-only dictionary that maps string property names to LogEventPropertyValue objects containing detailed property information and values. The formatted output is written to the provided TextWriter instance. An optional IFormatProvider parameter can control the specific formatting behavior of the output. If no format provider is supplied, the method defaults to using null as the format provider.

Converts a message template into a textual message using properties that match template tokens for substitution. The output parameter receives the resulting message text; if the properties mismatch with the template, the template returns with incomplete token substitution. The optional formatProvider parameter supplies culture-specific formatting information, or remains null. This method accepts three parameters: properties, output, and formatProvider. ArgumentNullException is thrown when either properties or output parameters are null.

Converts a message template into a textual message using properties that match the template's tokens. The method returns the message created from the template and the provided properties. If the properties are mismatched with the template, the template is returned with incomplete substitution. The formatProvider parameter supplies the culture-specific formatting information, or it may be null. Throws ArgumentNullException if either the properties parameter or the output parameter is null.

Configures the logger's maximum collection count setting. This method establishes the upper limit for the number of items the logger will collect and store during runtime operation. The maximumCollectionCount parameter specifies this specific limit as an integer value. Returns a LoggerConfiguration object to enable method chaining and fluent configuration API style.

Configures the maximum collection count limit for the logger configuration object instance. Sets the specified maximumCollectionCount parameter value on this LoggerConfiguration instance. This method supports fluent configuration patterns by returning the updated LoggerConfiguration object, enabling convenient method chaining for additional configuration operations, setup customization, and further logger configuration requirements and options.

When destructuring objects, collections are restricted to a specified maximum count, thereby preventing any bloated payloads. The limit is applied to each individual collection separately, meaning the combined sum of all collection lengths can exceed the specified overall maximum limit. This collection count restriction applies to all IEnumerable instances, including dictionaries.

When destructuring objects, all collections must be restricted to a specified maximum count, thus effectively avoiding unnecessary overall payload bloating concerns. Limits apply independently to each individual collection; the cumulative sum of all collection item lengths can potentially exceed the individual limit. This applies consistently to all IEnumerable implementations, including dictionaries.

GenReSTTree generates a complete reStructuredText tree structure documentation for a given Cobra command. It accepts a pointer to a cobra.Command object and a directory path string as input parameters. The function processes the entire command tree and generates comprehensive documentation in reStructuredText format within the specified output directory, returning an error if any generation operation fails during execution.

GenReSTTree generates a complete reStructuredText documentation tree for a Cobra command, recursively writing all documentation output to the specified target directory location. It accepts a cobra.Command pointer and directory path string as input parameters, returning an error if the generation operation fails. Useful for creating fully structured documentation from complete Cobra CLI command hierarchies and all nested subcommands.

GenReSTTree generates a ReST documentation page for a command and all its descendants in a specified directory. The function may not work correctly if your command names contain hyphens. If you have a command `cmd` with subcommands `sub` and `sub-third`, and `sub` also has a subcommand `third`, the output file `cmd-sub-third.1` may contain undefined or ambiguous help output.

GenReSTTree generates a ReST page for a command and all its descendants in the given directory. The function may not work correctly if command names have hyphens in them. If you have `cmd` with two subcmds, `sub` and `sub-third`, and `sub` has a subcommand called `third`, it is undefined which help output will be in the file `cmd-sub-third.1`.

The `if` conditional statement evaluates the predicate function `pred` with variable arguments `*w`. The predicate receives zero or more arguments unpacked from the parameter collection. Based on the predicate's return value, conditional execution branches to different code paths. The predicate function determines the truthiness of the condition being tested. Numeric values 0 through 4 may be used as argument indices or counts within the predicate evaluation and branching logic structure for control flow.

The `if` statement evaluates a predicate function with unpacked arguments from the parameter list. The predicate `pred` is invoked with unpacked values from `*w`, which accepts zero to four positional arguments. The conditional branch result is directly determined by the predicate's return value. This construct enables dynamic branching logic by applying the specified predicate function to a variable number of arguments, supporting flexible control flow and conditional execution patterns based on predicate results.

If the current window matches our predicate and we haven't reached our maximum number of replacements, splice in the substitutes and then consume all following windows that overlap with this one. For example, if the iterable is (0, 1, 2, 3, 4...) and the window size is 2, we have windows (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)... If the predicate matches (0, 1), we need to remove both (0, 1) and (1, 2).

PropertyEnricher Constructor

Initializes a new instance of PropertyEnricher with the specified property name and value.

Parameters:
- name (string): The name of the property to enrich.
- value (object): The value to associate with the property.

This constructor creates a PropertyEnricher that adds custom properties to log events. The name parameter identifies the property, while value contains the data to attach. The destructureObjects parameter controls whether nested objects are decomposed into constituent properties.

PropertyEnricher constructor creates a new PropertyEnricher instance with three parameters. The name parameter accepts a string value and is required; it uniquely identifies the property by name. The value parameter accepts an object and is required; it contains the property data to be stored. The destructureObjects parameter is an optional boolean flag that defaults to false. This flag controls how object values are handled during instance creation. Together, these parameters define the complete configuration and behavior of the PropertyEnricher instance.

Creates a new property enricher for the context. Accepts a property name, value, and optional destructureObjects flag. When true, non-primitive, non-array values are converted to structures; otherwise, unknown types convert to scalars (typically stored as strings). Returns a handle for later property removal. Throws ArgumentNullException if name is null, or ArgumentException if name is empty or whitespace-only.

Creates a new property enricher and returns a handle that enables later removal of the property from the enrichment context. Parameters include name (the required property name), value (the property value to be enriched), and destructureObjects (a Boolean flag that controls whether non-primitive, non-array type values are converted to structures or converted to scalar values, which are typically stored as strings). Throws ArgumentNullException if name is null or ArgumentException if name is empty or contains only whitespace.

The LogEvent constructor initializes a new instance with a timestamp, log level, optional exception, message template, and associated properties. The DateTimeOffset parameter specifies when the event occurred. LogEventLevel indicates the severity level. The Exception parameter captures error information if applicable. MessageTemplate defines the log message format. Properties is an enumerable collection of LogEventProperty objects linked to and describing the logged event.

The LogEvent constructor initializes a new log event instance with a timestamp, severity level, and exception. The messageTemplate parameter defines the log message format, while the properties parameter provides additional structured context data. The DateTimeOffset captures when the event occurred, LogEventLevel specifies the severity level, Exception holds error information if applicable, and IEnumerable<LogEventProperty> contains structured properties associated with the log event.

Constructs a new LogEvent instance with the specified parameters. Accepts: timestamp, indicating when the event occurred; level, specifying the event's level; exception, for an optional exception associated with the event; messageTemplate, describing the event; and properties, containing all event properties associated with the event including those presented in the messageTemplate parameter. Throws ArgumentNullException if either the messageTemplate or properties is null.

Constructs a new LogEvent instance. Parameters: timestamp (the time at which the event occurred), level (the severity level of the event), exception (an optional exception associated with the event, or null), messageTemplate (the message template describing the event), and properties (the properties associated with the event, including those presented in messageTemplate). Throws ArgumentNullException when either messageTemplate or properties parameter is null.

Configures a named property to be added to all subsequent log events created by the logger. The name parameter specifies the property identifier, while the value parameter provides the property content data. The destructureObjects parameter controls whether complex objects are decomposed into individual properties. Returns the LoggerConfiguration instance to enable fluent method chaining.

Configures a logger property with the specified name and value. The WithProperty method accepts a string parameter for the property name, an object parameter for the property value, and an optional boolean parameter destructureObjects that defaults to false, controlling whether objects are destructured in the logging. Returns a LoggerConfiguration instance for method chaining.

Includes the specified property value in all events logged to the logger. This method takes three parameters: the property name to add, the property value to add, and a destructureObjects flag (if true, unknown type objects are logged as structures; otherwise they are converted using object.ToString()). Returns a configuration object enabling method chaining.

The AtLevel method configures logger enrichment based on a specified log event level. It accepts a LogEventLevel parameter, enrichFromLevel, which defines the log level threshold from which enrichment will be applied. The method also accepts an Action<LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration> delegate, configureEnricher, that permits detailed configuration of enrichment-specific behavior and settings. The method returns a LoggerConfiguration instance, enabling fluent configuration chaining and allowing further customization of logger configuration settings through the fluent API pattern.

Configures logger enrichment that activates at a specified log event level threshold. The AtLevel method accepts a LogEventLevel parameter that determines the minimum threshold level at which enrichment rules are applied, and an Action<LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration> delegate that configures the specific enrichment behavior for that level. This enables conditional enrichment where the configured enrichers are invoked only for log events at or above the specified level. Returns a LoggerConfiguration instance to support fluent method chaining.

Apply an enricher only to log events with a LogEventLevel greater than or equal to the specified enrichFromLevel threshold value. This method permits additional information to be attached to warning and error events that might otherwise be too expensive to collect or store at the lower levels. The configureEnricher action parameter determines the wrapped enricher configuration and supports method chaining for fluent API configuration. ArgumentNullException is thrown if the configureEnricher parameter is null.

Apply an enricher to log events with a LogEventLevel at or above enrichFromLevel. This method permits attaching additional information to warnings and errors, which might be too expensive to collect or store at lower log levels. The enrichFromLevel parameter specifies the minimum log level threshold for enrichment processing. The configureEnricher parameter configures the wrapped enricher implementation. Returns a configuration object allowing for method chaining. Throws an ArgumentNullException if the configureEnricher parameter is null.

Creates a LogEventProperty instance with the specified name and value parameters. The name parameter defines the property identifier as a string value, while the value parameter contains the property data as an object type. The optional destructureObjects boolean parameter controls whether complex objects are recursively destructured during property creation and initialization; it defaults to false when not explicitly specified.

The name parameter identifies the property. The value parameter contains the data to log. The destructureObjects parameter determines whether to destructure nested objects. MessageTemplateTextFormatter is a class that implements the ITextFormatter interface for formatting message template text. It provides functionality to format text content according to message template specifications. By implementing ITextFormatter, this formatter integrates into the text formatting pipeline, enabling consistent handling of template-based text transformations across the application. The class supports standardized text formatting operations required by the interface contract.

MessageTemplateTextFormatter is a public class that implements the ITextFormatter interface. It provides text formatting functionality as defined by the ITextFormatter contract. This class can be used wherever ITextFormatter implementations are required, enabling polymorphic text formatting operations within the application's type system. As an implementer of ITextFormatter, MessageTemplateTextFormatter adheres to the interface's required methods and properties for text formatting operations.

An ITextFormatter that supports the Serilog message template format. Formatting log events for display has a different set of requirements and expectations from rendering the data within them. To meet this, the formatter overrides some behavior: First, strings are always output as literals (not quoted) unless some other format is applied to them. Second, tokens without matching properties are skipped rather than being written as raw text.

An ITextFormatter that supports the Serilog message template format. Formatting log events for display has different requirements and expectations than rendering the underlying data within them. The formatter overrides standard behavior in two ways: strings are always output as unquoted literals unless another format applies, and tokens without matching properties are skipped rather than written as raw text.

LogEventPropertyValueVisitor is a public abstract generic class with two type parameters: TState and TResult. The class serves as a foundational base for derived implementations to define custom behavior for handling log event property values. The TState parameter allows subclasses to maintain state during operations, while the TResult parameter enables specification of the appropriate return type. As an abstract class, LogEventPropertyValueVisitor cannot be instantiated directly but must be subclassed for concrete use.

LogEventPropertyValueVisitor is an abstract base class that provides a generic visitor pattern template for processing implementations. The generic type parameters TState and TResult enable flexible state management and return values during value traversal. Implementing classes define the specific visiting behavior for log event property values, allowing type-safe processing of event data through the visitor pattern. This design supports extensible and composable operations over property value hierarchies without modifying the underlying structures.

An abstract base class for visitors that walk or traverse data structures in the LogEventPropertyValue format. Subclasses can search for, transform, or print value structures by overriding appropriate methods. Stateless and specifically designed to accommodate allocation-free visiting of multiple values by the same visitor instance. A state object is passed through the entire visiting process, and each individual node generates its corresponding result upon being visited.

<summary>An abstract base class for visitors that traverse and process data in the LogEventPropertyValue format. Subclasses can override appropriate methods to search for, transform, or print the value structures being visited.</summary>
<remarks>Stateless and designed to accommodate allocation-free visiting of multiple values by the same visitor instance.</remarks>
<typeparam name="TState">The type of the state object that is passed through the entire visiting process.</typeparam>

Match is a method on the Router type that determines whether an HTTP request matches a specific route. It accepts an http.Request parameter and a RouteMatch pointer parameter. The method returns a boolean value: true if the request matches a route, or false if no matching route is found in the Router. The RouteMatch parameter provides access to the route matching results.

Match attempts to match the provided HTTP request against this router's defined routes, populating the provided RouteMatch with detailed information about any matched route. The method returns true if a matching route is found, false if no match occurs. The req parameter contains the HTTP request to match, while match receives the complete route information and details from any successful match attempt.

If a request does not match any route in this router or its subrouters, the function returns false. When a match failure reason is available, it is populated in the MatchErr field of the match argument. If the specific match failure type (e.g., not found) has a registered handler, that handler is assigned to the Handler field of the match argument.

If the request does not match any of the routes in this router or any of its subrouters, then the function returns false. Determines whether a serialize bound is required for a given field. This function evaluates a field definition and an optional variant context to decide if serialization trait bounds must be applied. Evaluates whether a serialize bound is required for a given attribute field based on its configuration and variant context. Accepts a reference to an attr::Field and an optional reference to an attr::Variant, allowing for variant-aware determination of serialization bounds. Returns a boolean value indicating whether the serialization bound is actually necessary for the specified field within the provided variant context.

Fields with a `skip_serializing` or `serialize_with` attribute, or which belong to a variant with a `skip_serializing` or `serialize_with` attribute, are not serialized by us, so we do not generate a bound. Fields with a `bound` attribute specify their own bound, so we do not generate one. All other fields may need a `T: Serialize` bound where T is the type of the field.

NewUUID generates and returns a new universally unique identifier (UUID) value. The function accepts no parameters. It returns two values: a UUID and an error. If UUID generation succeeds, the error return value will be nil; otherwise, it contains detailed information about the failure. Callers should always check the returned error value to ensure successful UUID generation before using the returned UUID value in their application logic and subsequent workflows or implementations.

NewUUID generates a new universally unique identifier and returns it along with an error value. The function takes no parameters. When successful, NewUUID returns the generated UUID paired with a nil error value. If generation fails, an error value is returned. The signature returns two values: a UUID and an error. This function is useful for applications that need to generate unique identifiers. The error value allows callers to handle generation failures.

NewUUID returns a Version 1 UUID based on the current NodeID, clock sequence, and the current time. If the NodeID has not been set by SetNodeID or SetNodeInterface, it will be set automatically. If the NodeID cannot be set, NewUUID returns nil. If the clock sequence has not been set by SetClockSequence, it will be set automatically. If GetTime fails to return the current time, NewUUID returns nil and an error.

The configureWrappedSink parameter provides an Action to configure the newly wrapped sink after wrapping. This helper method wraps sinks by accepting a parent sink configuration, a function for wrapping ILogEventSinks, and an action to configure the sinks for wrapping purposes. Returns an IDisposable that removes the pushed enrichers from the stack when disposed, supporting scope-based temporary enrichment of events. This static method enables adding enrichers at runtime without modifying the underlying logger configuration, providing flexible control over log event enhancement within specific execution contexts, code scopes, or async operations.

Pushes one or more log event enrichers onto the enrichment stack. Accepts a variable number of ILogEventEnricher instances through the params keyword argument, allowing multiple enrichers to be passed as individual arguments without requiring explicit array construction. Returns an IDisposable that, when disposed, removes the pushed enrichers from the stack and restores the previous enrichment state. This enables scoped enrichment contexts, supporting temporary addition of contextual data to log events within specific code regions or execution contexts.

ForContext is an extension method on ILogger that enables adding contextual information to log events with enhanced type safety. It accepts a LogEventLevel parameter to specify the severity level of the log event, a propertyName as a string identifier for the contextual property, and a value of generic type TValue. The destructureObjects parameter, which defaults to false, controls whether complex objects are destructured when recorded in the log entry. This method returns an ILogger instance, enabling fluent method chaining. The generic TValue parameter allows flexible property values while maintaining complete type safety throughout all logging operations.

Extension method for adding structured context properties to logger instances at specific event levels. The `ForContext<TValue>` generic method attaches a named property with the specified `propertyName` and `value` of any type directly to log events at the given `LogEventLevel`. The optional `destructureObjects` parameter controls whether complex objects are destructured into their individual component properties or logged as simple scalar values. This method enables enriching log output with contextual information for filtering and detailed analysis of logged events. Returns the `ILogger` instance, allowing method chaining for fluent configuration and composition of multiple context properties across logging operations.

Create a logger that enriches log events when the specified level is enabled.

Type parameter: TValue represents the type of the property value.

Parameters:
- logger: The logger instance.
- level: The log event level that determines whether to enrich logs with the property.
- propertyName: The property name; must be non-empty.
- value: The property value.
- destructureObjects: If true, serializes the value as a structured object when possible; if false, records the object as a scalar or simple array.

Returns: A logger configured to enrich log events as specified.

Exceptions: Throws ArgumentNullException when the logger parameter is null.

Creates a logger instance that enriches log events conditionally when the specified log level is enabled. Accepts the logger, a log event level to determine when enrichment should occur, a non-empty property name, the property value, and a destructureObjects parameter indicating how to serialize the value. When destructureObjects is true, the value will be serialized as a structured object if possible; otherwise, the object will be recorded as a scalar value or simple array. Returns a properly configured logger that will enrich log events with the specified property. Throws ArgumentNullException if the logger parameter is null.

Renders a collection of log event properties to a string representation. Accepts an IReadOnlyDictionary containing string keys mapped to LogEventPropertyValue instances. The optional IFormatProvider parameter enables culture-specific formatting behavior; when null, default formatting is applied. Returns the rendered string result based on the supplied properties and format provider configuration.

Renders a string representation of log event properties from a read-only dictionary mapping. Takes a dictionary with string keys mapping to LogEventPropertyValue objects as the properties parameter. Accepts an optional IFormatProvider to control culture-specific formatting of the output; this parameter defaults to null when not provided, using standard formatting conventions. Returns the complete formatted string representation of all provided log event properties.

<summary>Convert the message template into a text message using the supplied properties to replace matching template tokens.</summary>
<param name="properties">Properties that match the template tokens.</param>
<param name="formatProvider">Provides culture-specific formatting information, or null for default formatting.</param>
<returns>The text message created from the template and properties. If properties do not match template tokens, the template is returned with incomplete substitution.</returns>

Converts a message template into a textual message by substituting the supplied properties, which must match the template's tokens. The optional formatProvider parameter supplies culture-specific formatting information for the output. Returns the completed message created from the template and properties provided; if properties don't match the template tokens, returns the template with incomplete substitution. Raises ArgumentNullException when the properties parameter is null.

Parses a message template string into a MessageTemplate object. This public method accepts a single parameter named messageTemplate, which is a string containing the template content to be parsed. The method processes the input string and returns a new structured MessageTemplate instance representing the complete parsed result of the provided message template string.

Parses the message template string parameter and returns a structured MessageTemplate object. This method processes the input string by analyzing its syntax and template structure to construct a properly initialized MessageTemplate instance suitable for subsequent use. The returned object can be utilized for message evaluation, rendering, template variable substitution, and other related template operations throughout the system.

Parses the supplied message template. The message template to parse. A sequence of text or property tokens. When the template is not syntactically valid, text tokens are returned. The parser makes a best effort to extract and return all valid property tokens even in the presence of any parsing issues. Thrown when the parameter is null

Parses the supplied message template and returns a sequence of text or property tokens. Where the template is not syntactically valid, text tokens will be returned instead. The parser makes a best effort to extract valid property tokens even in the presence of parsing issues or errors. Throws an ArgumentNullException when the supplied messageTemplate parameter is null.

The AtLevel method configures logger behavior at a specified level using a LoggingLevelSwitch parameter. The method accepts a levelSwitch that dynamically controls the current logging level threshold, and a configureEnricher Action<LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration> parameter that applies enrichment configuration to the logger pipeline. This enables context-specific logging enrichment based on the active logging level without requiring static configuration rules. The method returns a LoggerConfiguration object instance, supporting fluent API chaining for continued configuration of additional logger setup options, decoration, output routing, and enrichment pipeline steps.

Configures logging at a specific level with enrichment options. The AtLevel method accepts a LoggingLevelSwitch parameter to control the logging level and an Action delegate that configures logger enrichment behavior. The configureEnricher parameter provides a LoggerEnrichmentConfiguration instance for setting up enrichers. This method returns a LoggerConfiguration instance, enabling method chaining for fluent configuration of complex logging pipelines. The LoggingLevelSwitch enables dynamic level adjustment at runtime, while the enrichment configuration allows adding enhanced context and other important diagnostic information to log output events.

Apply an enricher only to events with a LogEventLevel greater than or equal to the level specified by the levelSwitch parameter. A LoggingLevelSwitch object that specifies the level from which the enricher will be applied. An action that configures the wrapped enricher. Configuration object allowing method chaining. This method permits attaching additional information to warnings and error messages, information that might be too expensive to collect or properly store at the lower logging severity levels. Throws ArgumentNullException when configureEnricher parameter is null.

Apply an enricher only to events with a LogEventLevel greater than or equal to the level specified by the levelSwitch parameter. A LoggingLevelSwitch specifies the logging level from which the enricher will be applied. The configureEnricher action configures the wrapped enricher implementation. Returns a configuration object allowing method chaining. This method permits additional information to be attached to warnings and errors that might be too expensive to collect or store at lower priority log levels. It throws ArgumentNullException if configureEnricher is null.

uv_exepath

Gets the absolute filesystem path of the current executable. The function stores the path in the provided buffer and updates the size parameter with the actual path length. The size parameter should initially contain the maximum capacity of the buffer space. On success, it returns 0 and sets size to the actual path length. If the buffer is too small, the function returns an error code. This function is useful for locating resources relative to the executable's location or implementing self-referential program logic.

uv_exepath

Retrieves the absolute file path of the currently executing executable program.

Parameters:
- buffer: Character buffer that receives the executable path string.
- size: Pointer to size_t value. On input, specifies the buffer capacity in bytes. On output, receives the actual length of the executable path string in bytes, excluding the null terminator.

Returns:
An integer status code. Returns 0 on success. On error, returns a negative libuv error code. If the supplied buffer is too small, the size parameter is updated with the required capacity.

We avoid using a static buffer for path manipulations to prevent potential race conditions when this function is called by multiple consumers performing concurrent snprintf operations. AIX provides no direct mechanism for obtaining the executable path—neither the /procfs filesystem nor any standard libc APIs provide this necessary functionality. Instead, we carefully parse the pattern found in argv[0] and combine it with the PATH environment variable to accurately determine and fully construct the complete executable path for the running process.

We avoid using a static buffer for the path manipulations that occur outside the function because multiple consumers calling this function could potentially create race conditions when snprintf is used concurrently. AIX provides no direct method for determining or obtaining the executable path through either the /procfs filesystem or through any other available libc APIs. This approach therefore carefully parses the argv[0] pattern and uses it in conjunction with the PATH environment variable to correctly locate and construct the full executable path.

Establishes a conditional sink configuration for logger events. The Conditional method accepts a Func<LogEvent, bool> condition parameter that determines which log events are processed, and an Action<LoggerSinkConfiguration> configureSink parameter that configures the sink behavior. Log events are filtered through the condition before being sent to the fully configured sink. Returns the LoggerConfiguration for method chaining.

Configures a logger sink to be applied conditionally based on a predicate function. The condition parameter is a function that evaluates each log event and returns true to apply the sink configuration, false to skip it. The configureSink parameter defines the sink settings to apply when the condition is met. Returns the LoggerConfiguration object for method chaining.

Configures the sink to write LogEvents only when a specified condition evaluates to true. The condition parameter is a predicate that determines whether each LogEvent should be written to the configured sink. The configureSink parameter is an action configuring the wrapped sink. Returns a configuration object allowing method chaining. Throws ArgumentNullException when condition or configureSink is null.

Writes to a sink only when the supplied condition evaluates to true. The condition parameter is a predicate that determines when a LogEvent should be written to the configured sink. The configureSink parameter is an action that configures the wrapped sink. Returns a configuration object that allows method chaining. Throws ArgumentNullException if condition or configureSink is null.

NewHash generates a UUID using the provided hash function, a namespace UUID, and input data bytes. It accepts a hash.Hash interface implementation, a namespace UUID designated by the space parameter, a byte slice of data to be hashed, and a version integer parameter specifying the UUID protocol version. The function computes and returns a newly generated UUID based on all inputs.

NewHash generates a UUID by hashing the provided data using the specified hash function. It accepts four parameters: h (a hash.Hash implementation), space (a namespace UUID), data (bytes to hash), and version (the UUID version number). The function returns a UUID derived from the computed hash value. This enables namespace-based UUID generation with fully configurable hashing algorithms and version number specifications.

NewHash returns a new UUID derived from the hash of space concatenated with data generated by h. The hash must be at least 16 bytes in length. The first 16 bytes of the hash form the UUID. The UUID's version field is set to the lower 4 bits of the version parameter provided. NewHash is used to implement NewMD5 and NewSHA1.

NewHash returns a new UUID derived from the hash of space concatenated with data generated by h. The hash should be at least 16 bytes in length. The first 16 bytes of the hash are used to form the UUID. The UUID version will be the lower 4 bits of version. NewHash is used to implement NewMD5 and NewSHA1.

Determines whether a deserialize trait bound is required for a given field. Accepts a reference to an attr::Field and an optional attr::Variant for additional context. Returns a boolean value indicating whether the deserialize bound must be applied. This function analyzes the field's attributes and the variant's configuration to establish if a deserialization trait bound is necessary for proper code generation and overall functionality.

Determines whether a deserialize bound is required for a field during procedural macro code generation. Examines the field's attributes and any parent variant configuration to decide if a deserialization trait bound should be applied to the type. Takes a field reference and an optional variant reference as parameters, returning a boolean value that precisely indicates whether the bound is necessary for proper deserialization.

Fields with a `skip_deserializing` or `deserialize_with` attribute, or that belong to a variant with a `skip_deserializing` or `deserialize_with` attribute, are not deserialized by us so we do not generate a bound. Fields with a `bound` attribute specify their own bound so we do not generate one. All other fields may need a `T: Deserialize` bound where T is the type of the field.

Fields with a `skip_deserializing` or `deserialize_with` attribute, or fields in a variant with a `skip_deserializing` or `deserialize_with` attribute, are not deserialized, and we still do not generate any bound. Fields with a `bound` attribute explicitly specify their own bound, so we do not generate one. All other fields may still need a `T: Deserialize` bound where T is the type of the field.
